title: Guess what? Sēf has news
goal: Hear Sēf's news about the exam and react, using tara 'just so you know, mind you'
tip: tara flags news or a warning, like 'just so you know' or 'mind you'. Put it first: tara l-imtiḥān bāchir 'just so you know, the exam's tomorrow'; tara ana ma dhākart 'mind you, I haven't revised'. With wallāh it gets stronger: tara wallāh 'honestly, I mean it'.
grammar: discourse marker tara 'just so you know, mind you'
dialogue: A
سمعت؟ عندي لك خبر
simaʿt? ʿindi lak khabar
Have you heard? I've got news for you.
سِمَعْتْ؟ عِنْدِي لَكْ خَبَرْ
B
خير إن شاء الله؟ شو صار؟
khēr in shāʼ allāh? shu ṣār?
Good news, I hope? What's happened?
خَيْرْ إِنْ شَاءْ اللّٰهْ؟ شُو صَارْ؟
A
ترا الامتحان باكر، مب يوم الخميس!
tara l-imtiḥān bāchir, mub yōm il-khamīs!
Just so you know, the exam's tomorrow, not Thursday!
تَرَا الْاِمْتِحَانْ بَاكِرْ، مُبْ يَوْمْ الْخَمِيسْ!
B
صج؟ ما كنت أدري. منو قال لك؟
ṣij? ma kint adri. minu gāl-lak?
Really? I had no idea. Who told you?
صِجْ؟ مَا كِنْتْ أَدْرِي. مِنُو قَالْ لَكْ؟
A
طرشوا رسالة في القروب. ما شفتها؟
ṭarrashaw risāla fi l-grūb. ma shift-ha?
They sent a message in the group. Didn't you see it?
طَرَّشَوْا رِسَالَة فِي الْقْرُوبْ. مَا شِفْتْهَا؟
B
لا والله. ترا ما ذاكرت شي، لازم أذاكر!
la wallāh. tara ma dhākart shay, lāzim adhākir!
No, honestly. Mind you, I haven't revised a thing, I have to study!
لَا وَاللّٰهْ. تَرَا مَا ذَاكَرْتْ شَيْ، لَازِمْ أَذَاكِرْ!
A
ترا والله أنا بعد! خل نذاكر مع بعض الليلة
tara wallāh ana baʿad! khal ndhākir maʿa baʿaẓ il-lēla
Honestly, same here! Let's revise together tonight.
تَرَا وَاللّٰهْ أَنَا بَعَدْ! خَلْ نْذَاكِرْ مَعَ بَعَضْ اللَّيْلَة
items: just so you know, mind you (before news or a warning)
you'll see written ترى; tara ana ma adri = mind you, I don't know
have you heard? did you hear? (to a man)
to a woman: simaʿti? (سمعتي؟); I heard: simaʿt, said by men and women
I've got news for you (to a man)
to a woman: ʿindi lich khabar (عندي لج خبر); news: khabar (خبر)
I didn't know, I had no idea
you also know ma dirēt (ما دريت), 'I didn't realise'
to a woman: minu gāl-lich? (منو قال لج؟)
he sent: ṭarrash (طرش); you'll see written طرشو
I haven't revised, I didn't study (for an exam); you haven't revised (to a man)
to a woman (you haven't): ma dhākarti (ما ذاكرتي)

title: Looks like he's not coming
goal: Guess with Maryam at the office why the manager isn't in, using shakl- 'it looks like'
tip: shakl- with an ending means 'it looks like': shaklah 'looks like he…', shakli 'looks like I…', shaklich 'looks like you (f.)…'. A sentence follows: shaklah mub yāy 'looks like he's not coming'. To someone's face it is 'you look': shaklak taʿbān 'you look tired'.
grammar: discourse marker shakl- + ending: shaklah 'it looks like he…'
dialogue: A
صباح الخير! شكلك تعبان اليوم
ṣabāḥ il-khēr! shaklak taʿbān il-yōm
Good morning! You look tired today.
صَبَاحْ الْخَيْرْ! شَكْلَكْ تَعْبَانْ الْيَوْمْ
B
صباح النور. هيه، ما نمت عدل. وين المدير؟
ṣabāḥ in-nūr. hē, ma nimt ʿadil. wēn il-mudīr?
Good morning. Yes, I didn't sleep properly. Where's the manager?
صَبَاحْ النُّورْ. هَيْه، مَا نِمْتْ عَدِلْ. وَيْنْ الْمُدِيرْ؟
A
ما يا. شكله في اجتماع برا المكتب
ma yā. shaklah fi ijtimāʿ barra l-maktab
He hasn't come in. Looks like he's at a meeting outside the office.
مَا يَا. شَكْلَهْ فِي اِجْتِمَاعْ بَرَّا الْمَكْتَبْ
B
صج؟ شكله مب ياي اليوم. سيارته مب هني
ṣij? shaklah mub yāy il-yōm. sayyārtah mub hni
Really? Looks like he's not coming today. His car's not here.
صِجْ؟ شَكْلَهْ مُبْ يَايْ الْيَوْمْ. سَيَّارْتَهْ مُبْ هْنِي
A
صح. خلنا نخلص المشروع بدري!
ṣaḥḥ. khallna nkhalliṣ il-mashrūʿ badri!
Right. Let's get the project done early!
صَحّْ. خَلّْنَا نْخَلِّصْ الْمَشْرُوعْ بَدْرِي!
B
شكلج بتخلصين قبلي! وأنا شكلي بنام على المكتب
shaklich bitkhallṣīn gabli! w ana shakli banām ʿala l-maktab
Looks like you'll finish before me! And it looks like I'll fall asleep at my desk.
شَكْلِجْ بِتْخَلّْصِينْ قَبْلِي! وْأَنَا شَكْلِي بَنَامْ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبْ
A
لا تنام! ترا شكله ياي!
la tnām! tara shaklah yāy!
Don't fall asleep! Watch out, looks like he's coming!
لَا تْنَامْ! تَرَا شَكْلَهْ يَايْ!
items: it looks like he… / it…; he seems
about a woman or a feminine thing: shaklha (شكلها); on its own shakl means 'look, appearance'
it looks like he's not coming
about a woman: shaklha mub yāya (شكلها مب ياية)
it looks like I…, I think I'll…
shakli barūḥ = looks like I'll go
to a woman: shaklich taʿbāna (شكلج تعبانة)
it looks like you…, you look (to a woman)
I didn't sleep properly; you didn't sleep properly (to a man)
to a woman (you didn't): ma nimti ʿadil
don't fall asleep, don't sleep (to a man)
to a woman: la tnāmīn (لا تنامين)

title: So where do we eat, then?
goal: Change dinner plans with Sēf when the restaurant is shut, using ʿayal 'so, then' and māshi 'OK'
tip: ʿayal means 'so, then, in that case', following on from what was just said: ʿayal wēn? 'so where, then?', ʿayal lēsh? 'then why?'. After a word it means 'then': zēn ʿayal 'fine then', yalla ʿayal 'come on then'. māshi 'OK, fine' agrees to a plan.
grammar: discourse markers ʿayal 'so, then, in that case' and māshi 'OK, fine'
dialogue: A
هلا! كيف الشغل؟
hala! chēf ish-shughul?
Hi! How's work?
هَلَا! كَيْفْ الشُّغُلْ؟
B
هلا فيك. ماشي الحال. وين نتعشى الليلة؟
hala fīk. māshi l-ḥāl. wēn nitʿashsha l-lēla?
Hi. Not bad. Where are we having dinner tonight?
هَلَا فِيكْ. مَاشِي الْحَالْ. وَيْنْ نِتْعَشَّى اللَّيْلَة؟
A
ترا المطعم اللي نحبه مسكر اليوم
tara l-maṭʿam illi nḥibbah msakkar il-yōm
Just so you know, the restaurant we like is closed today.
تَرَا الْمَطْعَمْ اللِّي نْحِبَّهْ مْسَكَّرْ الْيَوْمْ
B
عيل وين نروح؟ المول زحمة الحين
ʿayal wēn nrūḥ? il-mōl zaḥma l-ḥīn
So where do we go, then? The mall's packed now.
عَيَلْ وَيْنْ نْرُوحْ؟ الْمَوْلْ زَحْمَة الْحِينْ
A
عيل ليش ما نطلب؟
ʿayal lēsh ma niṭlub?
Then why don't we order in?
عَيَلْ لَيْشْ مَا نِطْلُبْ؟
B
والله فكرة! زين عيل، بس انت تطلب، يصير؟
wallāh fikra! zēn ʿayal, bas inta tiṭlub, yṣīr?
Good idea! Fine then, but you're ordering, OK?
وَاللّٰهْ فِكْرَة! زَيْنْ عَيَلْ، بَسْ اِنْتَ تِطْلُبْ، يْصِيرْ؟
A
ماشي. يلا عيل، تعال عندي الساعة ثمان
māshi. yalla ʿayal, taʿāl ʿindi s-sāʿa thamān
OK. Come on then, come round to mine at eight.
مَاشِي. يَلَّا عَيَلْ، تَعَالْ عِنْدِي السَّاعَة ثَمَانْ
items: ʿayal lēsh ma…? = then why don't…?
come on then, let's go then
also 'walking, leaving': ana māshi = I'm off
not bad, it's going OK (about work, studies, things)
for 'how are you?' keep b-khēr, allāh ysallmak
closed, shut (a shop, a restaurant, a door)
with a feminine noun or a plural of things: msakkara (مسكرة); open: maftūḥ (مفتوح)
come round to mine, come to my place (to a man)

title: Oh, come on!
goal: Hold out against Sēf's push to go to the desert, with ʿād 'come on' and aṣlan 'anyway'
tip: ʿād adds push: yalla ʿād 'come on now', bas ʿād 'that's enough now', la ʿād 'oh, come on'. aṣlan is 'anyway, in the first place': ana aṣlan ma ʿindi jākēt. Friends talk fast: madri (ma adri), shallah (in shāʼ allāh), aani (yaʿni), ʿshān (ʿashān). Know them; say the full forms.
grammar: discourse markers ʿād 'come on, now' and aṣlan 'anyway'; fast speech
dialogue: A
يلا عاد! تعال ويانا البر الليلة
yalla ʿād! taʿāl wiyyāna l-barr il-lēla
Come on now! Come to the desert with us tonight.
يَلَّا عَادْ! تَعَالْ وِيَّانَا الْبَرّْ اللَّيْلَة
B
قلت لكم ما أقدر، لازم أذاكر
gilt-lkum ma agdar, lāzim adhākir
I told you lot I can't, I have to revise.
قِلْتْ لْكُمْ مَا أَقْدَرْ، لَازِمْ أَذَاكِرْ
A
بس عاد! كل أسبوع عندك امتحان
bas ʿād! kill usbūʿ ʿindak imtiḥān
Come off it! Every week you've got an exam.
بَسْ عَادْ! كِلّْ أُسْبُوعْ عِنْدَكْ اِمْتِحَانْ
B
وأصلا البر بارد الحين
w aṣlan il-barr bārid il-ḥīn
And anyway, the desert's cold now.
وْأَصْلًا الْبَرّْ بَارِدْ الْحِينْ
A
لا عاد، مب جي! الجو حلو
la ʿād, mub chī! il-jaww ḥilu
Oh come on, it's not like that! The weather's nice.
لَا عَادْ، مُبْ جِي! الْجَوّْ حِلُو
B
أنا أصلا ما عندي جاكيت
ana aṣlan ma ʿindi jākēt
I haven't even got a jacket, anyway.
أَنَا أَصْلًا مَا عِنْدِي جَاكَيْتْ
A
عيل بييب لك واحد. ترا بمر عليك!
ʿayal bayīb-lak wāḥid. tara bamurr ʿalēk!
Then I'll bring you one. And just so you know, I'm picking you up!
عَيَلْ بَيِيبْ لَكْ وَاحِدْ. تَرَا بَمُرّْ عَلَيْكْ!
items: now, then, come on (adds push or emphasis)
often after the word it pushes: yalla ʿād, bas ʿād; at the start it means 'well': ʿād ana ma adri = well, how would I know
that's enough now, come off it; stop it (friends only)
often with mub chī: la ʿād, mub chī!; before a verb it means 'don't … again': la ʿād tittaṣil = don't call again
anyway, in the first place, actually
I … anyway; I don't even … (with ma)
ana aṣlan ma ʿindi wagt = I haven't even got time
wider Gulf: mub chidhi (مب جذي); Kuwait: mū chidhi (مو جذي)

title: Nobody came!
goal: Complain to Maryam at work that nobody came to your project meeting, using maḥḥad 'nobody'
tip: maḥḥad means 'nobody'. It goes where the person would go, before the verb: maḥḥad yā 'nobody came', maḥḥad radd 'nobody answered'. After ma and a verb, use aḥad 'anybody': ma shift aḥad 'I didn't see anybody'.
dialogue: A
شو صار في اجتماع المشروع؟
shu ṣār fi ijtimāʿ il-mashrūʿ?
What happened at the project meeting?
شُو صَارْ فِي اِجْتِمَاعْ الْمَشْرُوعْ؟
B
محد يا! قعدت ساعة بروحي
maḥḥad yā! gaʿadt sāʿa b-rūḥi
Nobody came! I sat there for an hour on my own.
مَحَّدْ يَا! قَعَدْتْ سَاعَة بْرُوحِي
A
محد؟ صج؟ طرشت لهم في القروب؟
maḥḥad? ṣij? ṭarrasht-lhum fi l-grūb?
Nobody? Really? Did you message them in the group?
مَحَّدْ؟ صِجْ؟ طَرَّشْتْ لْهُمْ فِي الْقْرُوبْ؟
B
هيه، بس محد رد علي
hē, bas maḥḥad radd ʿalay
Yes, but nobody got back to me.
هَيْه، بَسْ مَحَّدْ رَدّْ عَلَيْ
A
غريبة! وترا محد قال لي شي بعد
gharība! w tara maḥḥad gāl-li shay baʿad
That's odd! And just so you know, nobody said a thing to me either.
غَرِيبَة! وْتَرَا مَحَّدْ قَالْ لِي شَيْ بَعَدْ
B
تدرين شو؟ شكله محد يهتم بالمشروع
tadrīn shu? shaklah maḥḥad yihtamm bil-mashrūʿ
You know what? Looks like nobody cares about the project.
تَدْرِينْ شُو؟ شَكْلَهْ مَحَّدْ يِهْتَمّْ بِالْمَشْرُوعْ
A
لا تحاتي، الأسبوع الياي بكون في الاجتماع
la tḥāti, il-usbūʿ il-yāy bakūn fi l-ijtimāʿ
Don't worry, next week I'll be at the meeting.
لَا تْحَاتِي، الْأُسْبُوعْ الْيَايْ بَكُونْ فِي الْاِجْتِمَاعْ
items: one word; with ma and a verb say aḥad: ma shift aḥad = I didn't see anybody
nobody answered me, nobody got back to me
yihtamm b- = to care about: yihtamm bil-mashrūʿ
I sat, I stayed; you sat (to a man)
to a woman (you sat): gaʿadti (قعدتي); UAE also: yalast (يلست)
I sent (it to) them, I messaged them; you messaged them (to a man)
to a woman (you sent): ṭarrashtī-lhum (طرشتي لهم)
as an exclamation always gharība!; describing a man or a masculine thing: gharīb (غريب), shay gharīb = something strange

title: Nothing in the fridge
goal: Tell Sēf, who drops round hungry, that there's nothing at all in your flat, with wala shay and wala wāḥid
tip: wala before a noun means 'not a single, not even', usually after ma: ma ishtarēt wala shay 'I didn't buy a thing'. On its own, wala shay! is 'nothing at all!' and wala wāḥid! 'not one!'. Don't mix it up with walla 'or'.
grammar: wala + noun 'not a single, not even': wala shay, wala wāḥid
dialogue: A
أنا يوعان! شو عندك أكل؟
ana yōʿān! shu ʿindak akil?
I'm starving! What food have you got?
أَنَا يَوْعَانْ! شُو عِنْدَكْ أَكِلْ؟
B
ولا شي! الثلاجة فاضية
wala shay! ith-thallāja fāẓya
Nothing at all! The fridge is empty.
وَلَا شَيْ! الثَّلَّاجَة فَاضْيَة
A
ولا شي؟ ولا حتى خبز؟
wala shay? wala ḥatta khubiz?
Nothing? Not even bread?
وَلَا شَيْ؟ وَلَا حَتَّى خُبِزْ؟
B
لا والله. ما اشتريت ولا شي، ولا مرة طبخت هني
la wallāh. ma ishtarēt wala shay, wala marra ṭabakht hni
No, honestly. I haven't bought a thing, I've never once cooked here.
لَا وَاللّٰهْ. مَا اِشْتَرَيْتْ وَلَا شَيْ، وَلَا مَرَّة طَبَخْتْ هْنِي
A
عيل نطلب. في مطعم مفتوح الحين؟
ʿayal niṭlub. fī maṭʿam maftūḥ il-ḥīn?
Then let's order. Is there a restaurant open now?
عَيَلْ نِطْلُبْ. فِي مَطْعَمْ مَفْتُوحْ الْحِينْ؟
B
ولا واحد! كلها مسكرة هني، الساعة ثنتين بالليل
wala wāḥid! killha msakkara hni, is-sāʿa thintēn bil-lēl
Not one! They're all shut round here, it's two in the morning.
وَلَا وَاحِدْ! كِلّْهَا مْسَكَّرَة هْنِي، السَّاعَة ثِنْتَيْنْ بِاللَّيْلْ
A
خلاص، بنام يوعان. بس ترا ولا كلمة حق أمي!
khalāṣ, banām yōʿān. bas tara wala kilma ḥagg ummi!
Fine, I'll go to bed hungry. But mind you, not a word to my mum!
خَلَاصْ، بَنَامْ يَوْعَانْ. بَسْ تَرَا وَلَا كِلْمَة حَقّْ أُمِّي!
items: nothing at all, not a thing
ma ishtarēt wala shay = I didn't buy a thing; not walla (ولّا, 'or')
not one, not a single one
for a feminine thing: wala waḥda (ولا وحدة)
wala ḥatta khubiz = not even bread
goes before a past verb: wala marra ṭabakht = I've never once cooked
open (a shop, a restaurant, a door)
with a feminine noun: maftūḥa (مفتوحة); closed: msakkar
plural things take the feminine: killha maftūḥa = they're all open
I cooked; you cooked (to a man)
to a woman (you cooked): ṭabakhti (طبختي); I cook: aṭbakh

title: Four in the morning? No way!
goal: Turn down Sēf's dawn trip out to sea with abad 'never, not at all', and find out about ghaṣb 'whether you like it or not'
tip: abad means 'never, not at all'. Use it with ma or la: ana abad ma aṣḥa arbaʿ 'I never get up at four', la abad 'no, not at all'. ghaṣb means 'by force': ghaṣb ʿannak 'whether you like it or not', ghaṣb ʿanni 'against my will, I couldn't help it'.
grammar: abad 'never, not at all' with ma or la; ghaṣb 'by force'
dialogue: A
باكر نطلع البحر الساعة أربع الصبح!
bāchir niṭlaʿ il-baḥar is-sāʿa arbaʿ iṣ-ṣubḥ!
Tomorrow we're going out to sea at four in the morning!
بَاكِرْ نِطْلَعْ الْبَحَرْ السَّاعَة أَرْبَعْ الصُّبْحْ!
B
أربع؟ لا لا، ما أقدر!
arbaʿ? la la, ma agdar!
Four? No, no, I can't!
أَرْبَعْ؟ لَا لَا، مَا أَقْدَرْ!
A
ليش؟ زعلان من الشباب؟
lēsh? zaʿlān min ish-shabāb?
Why? Are you cross with the guys?
لَيْشْ؟ زَعْلَانْ مِنْ الشَّبَابْ؟
B
لا أبد، بس أنا أبد ما أصحى أربع
la abad, bas ana abad ma aṣḥa arbaʿ
Not at all, I just never get up at four.
لَا أَبَدْ، بَسْ أَنَا أَبَدْ مَا أَصْحَى أَرْبَعْ
A
ولا مرة في حياتك؟ عيل هالمرة أول مرة!
wala marra fi ḥayātak? ʿayal hal-marra awwal marra!
Not once in your life? Then this time's the first time!
وَلَا مَرَّة فِي حَيَاتَكْ؟ عَيَلْ هَالْمَرَّة أَوَّلْ مَرَّة!
B
غصب يعني؟
ghaṣb yaʿni?
What, I don't get a choice?
غَصْبْ يَعْنِي؟
A
هيه، غصب عنك! بمر عليك الساعة ثلاث ونص
hē, ghaṣb ʿannak! bamurr ʿalēk is-sāʿa thalāth w nuṣṣ
Yes, like it or not! I'll pick you up at half past three.
هَيْه، غَصْبْ عَنَّكْ! بَمُرّْ عَلَيْكْ السَّاعَة ثَلَاثْ وْنُصّْ
items: never, not at all (with ma or la)
on its own as an answer: abad! = not at all!
no, not at all (it's nothing like that)
la abad, bas taʿbān = not at all, I'm just tired
ana abad ma aṣḥa arbaʿ = I never get up at four
in your life, ever (to a man)
to a woman: fi ḥayātich (في حياتج); in my life: fi ḥayāti
mub ghaṣb = you don't have to, nobody's forcing you; Kuwait: mū ghaṣb
what, I've got no choice? do I have to?
whether you like it or not (to a man) (friends only)
to a woman: ghaṣb ʿannich (غصب عنج); against my will, I couldn't help it: ghaṣb ʿanni (غصب عني)

title: I'm not going on my own!
goal: Put off Fahad's dinner plan: understand his māni 'I'm not' and answer with the Emirati mub
tip: māni means 'I'm not', before a describing word: māni fāhim 'I don't get it', māni rāyiḥ 'I'm not going'. Women say it too. You'll hear it most from Kuwaitis like Fahad. Emiratis mostly say mub: mub fāhim, mub fāẓi. Say mub; understand māni.
grammar: māni 'I'm not' (Kuwait-leaning) against Emirati mub + describing word
dialogue: A
هلا! إحنا بنروح نتعشى الليلة، شرايك؟
hala! iḥna binrūḥ nitʿashsha l-lēla, shrāyak?
Hi! We're going out for dinner tonight, how about it?
هَلَا! إِحْنَا بِنْرُوحْ نِتْعَشَّى اللَّيْلَة، شْرَايَكْ؟
B
هلا فيك. ترا أنا مب فاضي، عندي عرض باكر
hala fīk. tara ana mub fāẓi, ʿindi ʿarẓ bāchir
Hi. Mind you, I'm not free, I've got a presentation tomorrow.
هَلَا فِيكْ. تَرَا أَنَا مُبْ فَاضِي، عِنْدِي عَرْضْ بَاكِرْ
A
عرض؟ ماني فاهم، انت طالب مو موظف!
ʿarẓ? māni fāhim, inta ṭālib mū muwaẓẓaf!
A presentation? I don't get it, you're a student, not an employee!
عَرْضْ؟ مَانِي فَاهِمْ، اِنْتَ طَالِبْ مُو مُوَظَّفْ!
B
عرض في الشغل. بس مب فاهم المشروع، محد شرح لي
ʿarẓ fi sh-shughul. bas mub fāhim il-mashrūʿ, maḥḥad sharaḥ-li
A presentation at work. But I don't get the project, nobody explained it to me.
عَرْضْ فِي الشُّغُلْ. بَسْ مُبْ فَاهِمْ الْمَشْرُوعْ، مَحَّدْ شَرَحْ لِي
A
عيل ماني رايح بروحي! سيف مو فاضي بعد
ʿayal māni rāyiḥ b-rūḥi! Sēf mū fāẓi baʿad
Then I'm not going on my own! Sēf's not free either.
عَيَلْ مَانِي رَايِحْ بْرُوحِي! سَيْفْ مُو فَاضِي بَعَدْ
B
عيل نروح باكر بعد العرض. اليوم أبد ما أقدر
ʿayal nrūḥ bāchir baʿd il-ʿarẓ. il-yōm abad ma agdar
Then let's go tomorrow after the presentation. Today I can't at all.
عَيَلْ نْرُوحْ بَاكِرْ بَعْدْ الْعَرْضْ. الْيَوْمْ أَبَدْ مَا أَقْدَرْ
A
زين، باكر. بس ترا غصب عنك!
zēn, bāchir. bas tara ghaṣb ʿannak!
OK, tomorrow. But mind you, you're coming, like it or not!
زَيْنْ، بَاكِرْ. بَسْ تَرَا غَصْبْ عَنَّكْ!
items: men and women both say it; Emiratis say it too, but mostly ana mub (أنا مب)
I don't get it, I don't understand (Kuwait) (said by a man)
a woman says: māni fāhma (ماني فاهمة); UAE: mub fāhim (مب فاهم)
I'm not going (Kuwait) (said by a man)
a woman says: māni rāyḥa (ماني رايحة); UAE: mub rāyiḥ (مب رايح)
a woman: mū fāẓya (مو فاضية); UAE: mub fāẓi (مب فاضي)
(I) don't get it, (I'm) not following (said by a man)
a woman says: mub fāhma (مب فاهمة); Kuwait: māni fāhim
(I'm) not free, (I'm) busy (said by a man)
a woman says: mub fāẓya (مب فاضية); Kuwait: mū fāẓi, māni fāẓi
what do you think? how about it? (to a man)
to a woman: shrāyich? (شرايج؟); to a group: shrāykum?
